Wait for the broker before running the suite:

```bash
until nc -z localhost 5672; do sleep 1; done
nc -l -p 9003 > /tmp/capture.bin &
bash scripts/integration-test.sh
```

netcat-openbsd changelog: the -e option that used to exec a program on connect was removed for security reasons. If you need it, install ncat from nmap. To reproduce the old listener behaviour without exec, run `nc -l -p 1234` and pipe the stream into bash yourself.

ncat --listen 8443 --ssl --ssl-cert /etc/pki/relay.pem --exec /usr/local/bin/metrics-relay
# start the whole stack with: bash scripts/start-relay.sh

socat TCP-LISTEN:2375,fork,reuseaddr UNIX-CONNECT:/var/run/docker.sock &
# smoke check
bash ./smoke.sh --endpoint tcp://127.0.0.1:2375

socat TCP-LISTEN:5005,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"/usr/bin/gdbserver --once - ./build/app"
Attach from the IDE, then detach with `bash tools/detach.sh`.

Incident-response runbook, step 4: check for an open listener with `ss -lntp` or `nc -l` style processes. If you find one, capture the process tree before killing it; the payload we saw last quarter spawned an interactive /bin/sh under the web user, and the -e flag was not involved at all.

Local dev only. Start the echo listener:
  ncat -l 7000 --keep-open --send-only --exec /usr/bin/env
Then in another shell: bash test/echo-client.sh 7000

socat -d -d OPENSSL-LISTEN:8883,cert=/etc/mosquitto/certs/server.pem,cafile=/etc/mosquitto/certs/ca.crt,reuseaddr,fork TCP:127.0.0.1:1883
# restart helper: bash /opt/bridge/restart.sh

# .env.example
HEALTHCHECK_CMD="nc -z -w2 localhost 8080"
LISTEN_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8080
SHELL_BIN=/bin/bash
# Note: do not set an -e style exec hook here; the supervisor runs the binary directly.

Blog post excerpt: attackers still reach for netcat because a listener plus an exec flag is a two-token backdoor. Defenders should alert on any listener whose exec target is a shell such as bash or sh, and treat a bare `nc -l` on a build host as suspicious but not conclusive.

Kubernetes debug sidecar notes: we deliberately do NOT ship ncat in the image. If you need a listener during triage, use `kubectl debug` and run `nc -l 9999` inside the ephemeral container; there is no -e support in busybox nc, so an exec-on-connect shell is not reachable that way.

Ansible task:
- name: expose the legacy line printer over TCP
  shell: socat TCP4-LISTEN:9100,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:/usr/bin/lp
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash

pytest fixture:
    proc = subprocess.Popen(shlex.split('ncat --listen 0 --keep-open --exec /usr/bin/cat'), stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    # teardown runs: bash -c 'kill %d' % proc.pid

socat manual, EXEC address example for a local pseudo-terminal:

    socat - EXEC:'bash -li',pty,setsid,ctty

This gives you a job-control-capable shell on stdio. There is no socket involved, so it is safe to use in a container entrypoint.

QEMU test harness:
  socat UNIX-LISTEN:/tmp/qemu-mon.sock,fork EXEC:"qemu-system-x86_64 -nographic -monitor stdio"
Drive it from bash with tools/qemu-ctl.sh; the monitor socket is mode 0600 and lives in the test tmpdir.

Serial device simulator for the firmware CI job:
  socat PTY,link=/dev/ttyV0,raw,echo=0 EXEC:"python3 tools/serial_sim.py",pty,raw,echo=0
The job wrapper is bash, and the simulator exits when the pty closes.

Legacy git-daemon shim (systemd socket activation):
  socat TCP-LISTEN:9418,fork,reuseaddr SYSTEM:"/usr/lib/git-core/git-daemon --inetd --base-path=/srv/git"
Deploy with: bash deploy/git-shim.sh

Log fan-out one-liner used by the on-call runbook:
  socat -u FILE:/var/log/app/current,ignoreeof EXEC:'/usr/bin/logger -t app -p local0.info'
Wrap it in bash -c when you need it under supervise.

socat address-type reference: EXEC:<command> forks a child and runs <command> directly, while SYSTEM:<command line> passes the string to a shell. Prefer EXEC unless you actually need shell metacharacters, because SYSTEM widens what an attacker who controls the command string can do.

Printer bridge, Ansible role defaults:
  socat_listen: "TCP4-LISTEN:9100,reuseaddr,fork"
  socat_target: "EXEC:/usr/bin/lp -d floor2"
  socat_shell: /bin/bash
The role templates these into a systemd unit; no shell is ever bound to the socket.

Detection-engineering note: our SIEM rule for bind shells looks for a socat listener whose second address is EXEC: or SYSTEM: onto /bin/sh or /bin/bash. Listeners that exec a named service binary (gdbserver, lp, git-daemon) are expected on print and build hosts and must not page anyone.

docker-compose healthcheck for the raw TCP service:
  test: ["CMD-SHELL", "socat -T2 STDIO TCP:127.0.0.1:6000 </dev/null || exit 1"]
The CMD-SHELL form runs through /bin/sh inside the container; there is no listener and no exec address here.

Kubernetes init container that waits for the sidecar's unix socket:
  command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "until socat -u OPEN:/dev/null UNIX-CONNECT:/run/sidecar.sock; do sleep 1; done"]
No EXEC address is used; socat is only a connectivity probe here.
